email.body1:
Andrew, saw Casepoint advanced its platform unification across eDiscovery, investigations, and FOIA with new AI capabilities.

When the product surface expands like that, the bottleneck usually moves to signal-to-action: more in-market accounts surfacing than the team can act on in time. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Casepoint off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Andrew, quick follow-up for Casepoint.

From a RevOps seat, the cost is rarely the signals themselves, it's the latency between a signal firing and a rep actually touching the account, and that lag is exactly where measurable pipeline quietly leaks out before anyone notices.

Worth 15 minutes? I'll walk you through a teardown of your current outbound and three specific things I'd change. Our best practices alone usually lift response rates 50 to 70 percent.
email.body3:
Andrew, last bit of proof for Casepoint.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Casepoint's reply rate likely compares to other B2B software companies. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Andrew, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If tightening signal-to-action latency isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Unifying a platform is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your RevOps motion? I'll tailor it to Casepoint either way.
